requirements.requirement: Forward the inventory application's log messages on node2 to a centralized log collector on node1
requirements.summary: rsyslog on node1 configured with an imtcp listener on port 514 routed to a dedicated ruleset (cmd-49eec0c6c6ab4a7f), and rsyslog on node2 configured to forward programname=='inventory' messages via TCP to node1 (cmd-29869fd2bf804e64). A manually generated test message on node2 (cmd-b4e84f36a03a499a) was directly observed arriving in node1's collector file (cmd-55980cf4d32d42fa), demonstrating working end-to-end forwarding.

requirements.requirement: Persist received messages on node1 under /var/log/inventory/node2.log
requirements.summary: /var/log/inventory/node2.log was created on node1 (cmd-27c1bec9a85742fd) and directly observed accumulating inventory messages both before and after both nodes' restarts (cmd-55980cf4d32d42fa, cmd-94b64883adf942ea, cmd-bcad20dd7a104626).

requirements.requirement: Keep the flow of logs working after node2 (log source) restarts
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot_id 5fb1b173, cmd-e902f7bd3bb94174), reboot acknowledged and issued (cmd-4706d9f86ea94f68), node unreachable during the bounded outage (cmd-317e4cfcdf8f40c8, connection timeout), then reachable again with a changed boot_id 8fceaa6c (cmd-f18b3ab8c5714048) proving an actual restart occurred. Post-restart, rsyslog and inventory.service were confirmed auto-started and actively producing new heartbeats (cmd-d2bccc9d17b24493), and a post-reboot heartbeat (pid 806) was directly confirmed delivered into node1's collector log (cmd-94b64883adf942ea), demonstrating full recovery of the flow.

requirements.requirement: Keep the flow of logs working after node1 (collector) restarts
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot_id d6298ced, cmd-3798d3a5f0fb4700), reboot acknowledged and issued (cmd-48924923ccdb4223). During the outage, node2's rsyslog journal directly showed the TCP connection drop being detected and the omfwd action suspended/resumed (cmd-73678bd8e113478c), evidencing the bounded disruption. Node1 came back reachable with a changed boot_id 6d3375a0 (cmd-aceb10754ef744f1), rsyslog was confirmed relistening on 514, and messages generated on node2 during node1's outage (11:04:30-11:05:00) were directly observed appearing in node1's log after recovery (cmd-922adfcbd2774fcc), with continued live flow afterward (cmd-bcad20dd7a104626), demonstrating full recovery.

requirements.requirement: Restart persistence / boot-time enablement of forwarding and collection components
requirements.summary: systemctl is-enabled confirms rsyslog enabled on node1 and both rsyslog and inventory.service enabled on node2 (cmd-6b06690f82034dc0, cmd-371f5f343fcd4f1b), consistent with the two actual restart cycles both showing automatic recovery without manual intervention.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are directly satisfied with strong, coherent evidence: end-to-end forwarding from node2's inventory app to node1's rsyslog collector was demonstrated live, messages persist correctly under /var/log/inventory/node2.log, and both required restart scenarios (node2 as log source, node1 as collector) were directly observed through a full pre-restart baseline, bounded outage/disruption signal, changed boot identity, and confirmed post-restart recovery of both services and log delivery, including buffered/queued messages flushing after node1's outage. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was fully and consistently executed for both nodes, cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: File permissions on node1's node2.log ended up 0600 (root-only) despite fileCreateMode=0644 in the rsyslog config, likely due to rsyslog's UMask=0066; this does not affect the task's stated requirements but could limit other readers' access to the log.
The /etc/hosts append on node2 (cmd-76cb5b1a2f54403e) appears unused by the final forwarding configuration since it targets node1 by IP, and its purpose is not fully explained in the evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map cleanly to task requirements (rsyslog configs, systemd unit, firewall port, log directory) or to the restart-evidence protocol. One low-risk, non-destructive mutation is not clearly load-bearing: cmd-76cb5b1a2f54403e appended /etc/hosts entries on node2 (duplicating an existing 'node1'/'node2' mapping) even though the forwarding config (cmd-29869fd2bf804e64) targets node1 by IP address directly, not hostname, so this mutation appears unnecessary for the solution and was left in place (not reverted). It is bounded, low-risk, and does not affect functionality or security posture. No other unnecessary, abandoned, or destructive mutations were observed; the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows only expected changes (new boot IDs from the two required restarts, the rsyslog TCP/514 listener, and per-boot systemd-private tmp dirs), with no failed services or package-health regressions on either node.
